covers.quote: Only use brackets if you can remove the enclosed text and the meaning does not change.

rules.quote: Sentences must be grammatically correct if you remove the text in brackets.
rules.violation_condition: a sentence containing bracketed text that would not be grammatically complete or correct if the bracketed text were removed

rules.quote: These are specialist uses, so don’t use them in most content.
rules.violation_condition: curly brackets or slant brackets used in non-specialist, general content
when: Specialist fields such as mathematics and linguistics are exempt.
rules.why: Clear prohibition on curly and slant brackets in general prose.

covers.quote: Avoid using square brackets in parentheses
Reword the text to avoid square brackets inside of parentheses wherever possible.
Instead, use square brackets if you must put parenthetical information within parentheses.

examples.note: Uses square brackets for nested parenthetical information.

parts.quote: Australia’s Parliament House (architects Mitchell/Giurgola & Thorp [New York]) opened on 9 May 1988.

examples.note: Uses nested parentheses.

parts.quote: Australia’s Parliament House (architects Mitchell/Giurgola & Thorp (New York)) opened on 9 May 1988.

rules.quote: Don’t use sets of parentheses inside each other.
rules.violation_condition: a pair of parentheses nested directly inside another pair of parentheses
when: If parenthetical information must be enclosed within parentheses, use square brackets instead.
rules.why: G-2, G-4: Consolidated prohibition against nested parentheses and the preference/exception to use square brackets or reword.

examples.note: No comma follows the closing bracket.

parts.quote: The winning tenderer (a local company) signed the contract on Tuesday.

examples.note: Erroneous comma placed after closing bracket between subject and verb.

parts.quote: The winning tenderer (a local company), signed the contract on Tuesday.

rules.quote: A comma follows a closing bracket only if you would have used a comma if there were no brackets.
rules.violation_condition: a comma placed immediately after a closing bracket where no comma would be grammatically required without the bracketed phrase
rules.why: G-2: Specific actionable punctuation rule with compliant and violating examples.

examples.note: Full sentence in parentheses has period inside the closing bracket.

parts.quote: The department was in a heritage-listed building. (The building was designed by award-winning architect Enrico Taglietti.)

rules.quote: If the content inside the brackets is a full sentence, include the end punctuation inside the brackets.
rules.violation_condition: bracketed text that forms a complete sentence standalone where the terminating punctuation is placed outside the closing bracket rather than inside
when: The bracketed content is an independent full sentence.

examples.note: Rewritten as two separate sentences.

parts.quote: The winning tenderer signed the contract on Tuesday. They were a local company.

examples.note: Parenthetical insertion reduced to a phrase rather than a full sentence.

parts.quote: The winning tenderer (a local company) signed the contract on Tuesday.

examples.note: A full sentence enclosed in parentheses inside another sentence.

parts.quote: The winning tenderer (They were a local company.) signed the contract on Tuesday.

rules.quote: Don’t use brackets to enclose a sentence within a sentence. Rewrite the text instead.
rules.violation_condition: a complete standalone sentence enclosed in brackets within another sentence
rules.why: Specific, actionable syntactic rule with explicit compliant and violating examples.

covers.quote: Write brackets in the same type as the surrounding text

examples.note: Parentheses match the roman surrounding text rather than italics.

rules.quote: Brackets should be in the same type (roman, italics, bold) as the text around the brackets. This is regardless of the type of the text inside the brackets.
rules.violation_condition: brackets formatted in italics or bold when the surrounding text outside the brackets is roman (or not sharing the surrounding typeface)
